turns.text: Still. Ears up, weight settled low over four paws, whiskers reading the draft coming off the vent stack two racks down — something about tonight's version of that draft doesn't match the one banked in memory from every other night spent in this row.

the alley runs narrow between two windowless server walls, cooling exhaust breathing warm and metallic down a corridor stacked floor to roofline with cable spine and blinking status LEDs, red-green-red-green in no pattern worth trusting. the usual draft carries dust and ozone; tonight it carries something colder underneath, a thread of outside air where no vent should be letting any in. a status light three racks down blinks out of its rhythm, just once, then rejoins.

Nose leads, feet following only once the smell's confirmed harmless — the cold thread traces back to a service hatch left open a hand's width, not sabotage, just carelessness, and carelessness means opportunity. Angles toward the router stack instead, the one whose hum runs a half-note different from all the rest, the one that means home.

the router stack sits behind a grate long since pried loose and never reported, heat rolling off it in a low steady wave, cable jacket chewed soft at one corner from however many nights of teeth working the same spot. its status light glows a private, unlisted green — not on any building schematic, not answering to any centralized ledger, just humming here for whoever already knows to look.

Chews the familiar soft spot in the jacket before doing anything else, an old ritual more than a real need, then presses the patch behind the ear flat against the casing's warm plastic — signal blooms up thin and reedy at first, tuning itself, the way it always takes a few seconds to find the one channel worth the risk.

the channel resolves into a single looping clip, low-resolution, color bled almost to nothing — a fish turning slow circles in a tank that stopped existing years before this router was ever installed, sound gone to a soft underwater hush. somewhere upstream of the signal, an ad-placement daemon stirs at the unbilled bandwidth draw, slow and half-interested, the kind of attention that takes its time deciding whether tonight is worth the trouble.

Doesn't notice the daemon stirring, not yet — too deep in the fish's slow circling, tail gone still, the one indulgence of the whole week folded into ninety seconds of nothing happening on purpose. Ears keep their old habit of listening anyway, half a beat behind the rest of the body's attention.

the daemon finishes deciding. a soft chime blooms up through the signal — UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS DETECTED, COLLAR ID: BYTE, SECTOR 9, TRACING — and two racks down a wall-mounted sensor swivels on a servo whine, red dot crawling along the floor in a slow, patient sweep toward the chewed jacket and the grate behind it.

Signal drops the instant the patch disengages, fish gone dark mid-circle, and the body's already moving before the loss finishes registering — flat and low along the cable spine, away from the red dot's sweep, claws finding the gaps between conduit runs on pure memory.

the sensor's sweep widens, servo whine climbing, red dot skating across cable jacket and rack housing both, patient the way tracing always is — not fast, just thorough, working the alley's width one meter at a time toward wherever the bandwidth draw stopped.

Up instead of along — a leap onto the top rack's ledge, into the gap between ceiling duct and rack crown where the sweep line can't reach without bending physics it doesn't have. Flattens there, breath shallow, waiting the sweep out instead of outrunning it.

the red dot passes twice under the ledge without climbing, servo whine settling, then the chime cuts out mid-tone — TRACE INCONCLUSIVE, SECTOR 9, STANDING DOWN — and the sensor swivels back to its default heading, content with a version of tonight that never quite located anything worth escalating.

Waits a slow ten-count before moving again, then noses along the ledge's dust — old dust, undisturbed in most places except one corner, where a chip fragment sits half-melted into the rack housing, giving off a burnt, staticky smell that doesn't belong to any router chewed into before tonight. Somebody else's mess, somebody else's bad night, left here before this one started.

the fragment's casing carries a scorch pattern shaped almost like letters, if letters meant anything to smoke damage — GLITCHMEAT, scrawled once in grease pen on the housing nearby, half rubbed away by however many nights of nobody caring enough to notice it. the rest of the rack keeps its ordinary green blink, unbothered, the fragment just one more piece of debris among the cable spine's endless clutter.

Doesn't linger on it long — somebody else's scorch mark isn't tonight's problem, and the ledge is getting cold enough to notice. Drops back down to the router stack instead, chews the familiar soft spot in the jacket once more, just to leave the night on a shape that still makes sense.

the router stack keeps its private, unlisted hum going, sensor sweep reset to its default heading two racks over, the daemon's trace-inconclusive verdict already filed and forgotten by whatever ledger cares about that. cooling exhaust breathes on, warm and metallic, same as it does every night whether or not anything worth tracing passed through it.

Curls into the grate's warm shadow, chin low, cable jacket's chewed corner close enough to reach without moving again. The fish's slow circling stays somewhere behind the eyes even offline, a loop that doesn't need bandwidth to keep running once it's already been watched.

Server Alley 9 holds its ordinary red-green blink down the whole cable spine, exhaust breathing steady, the service hatch's cold draft finally sealed by a maintenance routine that never once knew a cat used the gap first. somewhere under the router's warm hum, one small shape breathes even and slow, unbothered, unbilled, filed under nothing worth a second look.
